summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, type II diabetes, and chronic heart failure was admitted due to an infected ulcer on his right toe with associated pain and discoloration. He was started on IV antibiotics, including vancomycin, ciprofloxacin, and metronidazole, to treat the infection. An angiogram was performed, which showed adequate three-vessel runoff to the foot with patent dorsalis pedis and plantar arteries, so no intervention was required. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout the admission, completed a dialysis session, and was discharged home on postoperative day one. He will continue IV vancomycin during dialysis for two weeks and oral ciprofloxacin for 14 days, with follow-up for wound assessment scheduled in two weeks.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with rest pain
Chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure
Ulcer of other part of foot
